gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the lowest battery voltage a solar maintainer's controller needs before it will start charging. OptiMate's own pages give 4 V for the lithium-capable Solar DUO 20W (TM522-D2) and 1 V for the lead-acid-only Solar 20W (TM522-2). So a battery that has been run nearly or fully flat may get no charge from the panel at all.
standout_why: I opened three rival pages. energyforthetaking.com/best-12v-solar-battery-charger-maintainer covers panel sizing against a 20–50 mA parasitic drain and says LiFePO4 needs a profile with no float stage, but it gives no start voltage and says nothing about cigarette-lighter sockets or night drain. solarbatteryscout.com/best-solar-battery-maintainer says it is AI-generated and has none of these mechanisms. gopowersolar.com's 10W-vs-20W post comes closest: it says LiFePO4 must not be charged below freezing and that the BMS 'will disconnect at low voltage'. It still gives no maintainer start-voltage figure. ChatGPT's own answer only says a maintainer 'won't reliably recover a severely discharged battery', with no number. The SUNER manual pages on manuals.plus and manualsee returned 403 or unreadable PDF data, and the SUNER product pages returned 429, so I could not check whether they state a threshold.
decides: This confirms the plan works only on a battery that already has some voltage left. If the battery may sit long enough to go very flat, or for lithium packs (a 12 V LiFePO4 that has gone into BMS low-voltage disconnect), choose a maintainer with a stated low start voltage and a lithium mode, then check the battery's voltage before relying on the panel. Among the products I could source, the OptiMate Solar DUO is the only one with a published start threshold (4 V) and dark-hours draw (under 0.5 mA). I could not source the same figures for the SUNER, VEVOR or Battery Tender units that ChatGPT showed. That is a gap in their documentation, not proof that they perform worse.
candidates: SUNER POWER 12W Solar Battery Charger Maintainer Ultra
SUNER POWER BC-20W Solar Battery Charger Ultra

findings.label: Lowest battery voltage at which charging starts ('Low Volt Start')
findings.note: Maker's page: 'SAVE: Low Volt Start of 4V'. It saves flat batteries 'from as low as 4V'. The page does not say whether it can wake a LiFePO4 whose BMS has cut off its terminals.

findings.label: Battery chemistries supported
findings.value: 12 V lead-acid and 12.8 V / 13.2 V LiFePO4 (4-series LFP only)
findings.note: Maker's page names the system voltages but gives no absorption or float setpoints and no low-temperature lithium cutoff. The FAQ on the related Solar 20W page says the DUO is 'suitable ONLY for 4 series cell Lithium Ferrous Phosphate or Lithium Iron Phosphate batteries'.

findings.label: Current drawn from the battery in the dark (monitor mode)
findings.note: Maker's spec: 'Draws less than 0.5mA during monitor mode'. That is at most 0.012 Ah/day (0.5 mA × 24 h).

findings.label: Lowest rated operating temperature
findings.note: This is a general operating limit for the controller, not a lithium charge cutoff.

findings.label: Lowest battery voltage at which charging starts ('Low Volt Start')
findings.note: Maker's spec sheet: 'Low Volt Start of 1V'. Recovers 'dead flat' sulphated batteries 'from as low as 1V'. Lead-acid only (STD/AGM/GEL, 2–240 Ah). Panel 22 V max, average output 1.66 A max with 3–5 A pulses. The maker's site files this model under 'Obsolete'.

findings.label: Solar controller start condition (charge-controller maker's own words)
findings.value: Charging starts when PV voltage is 5 V above battery voltage and continues while it stays 1 V above
findings.source_title: 8. Troubleshooting – Victron SmartSolar MPPT 75/10 up to 100/20 manual
findings.note: Victron is not one of the candidates. It is quoted for the mechanism. The same page: the charger 'should activate as soon it receives power from the battery, the PV supply, or both', and a lithium BMS can switch the charger off 'due to full batteries or low temperatures (below ~5°C)'.

findings.label: LiFePO4 cold-charging and BMS low-voltage disconnect (closest rival coverage)
findings.value: LiFePO4 must not be charged below freezing; the BMS disconnects at low voltage
findings.source_title: Solar Trickle Charger for RV Battery Storage: 10W vs 20W
findings.note: This page was among ChatGPT's results but not cited. It is the rival that already covers part of this angle. It gives no maintainer start-voltage threshold. It sizes panels with watts × peak sun hours × 0.7 ÷ 12.8 V: about 1–3 Ah/day from 10 W in winter, against 3.6–7 Ah/day drawn by an RV with its disconnect left on.
